hints: Focus on what density really means here, mass of gas in a fixed volume, so start from the ideal gas equation.
Remember fluorine exists as diatomic $\text{F}_2$, so $M_r = 38.0$, and convert $32^{\circ}\text{C}$ to $305\text{ K}$.
Find the volume of one mole under these conditions with $V = RT/p$, then divide $38.0\text{ g}$ by that volume to get density in $\text{g dm}^{-3}$.
walkthrough:
**Identify the gas and convert the temperature**

Fluorine is diatomic, so we use $\text{F}_2$ not F. That gives $M = 38.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

Temperature must be in kelvin:
$$T = 32 + 273 = 305\text{ K}$$

**Link density to the ideal gas equation**

Density is mass divided by volume. The ideal gas equation gives us volume from moles:
$$pV = nRT$$
For $n = 1\text{ mol}$:
$$V = \frac{RT}{p}$$

**Calculate the molar volume then the density**

Put in $R = 8.31\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$ and $p = 100000\text{ Pa}$:
$$V = \frac{8.31 \times 305}{100000} = 0.02535\text{ m}^3 = 25.35\text{ dm}^3$$
This is the volume of $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{F}_2$.

Density is mass of $1\text{ mol}$ divided by this volume:
$$\text{density} = \frac{38.0}{25.35} \approx 1.5\text{ g dm}^{-3}$$

options.A: Incorrect. $1.4\text{ g dm}^{-3}$ is what you get if you use $M_r = 35.5$, the $M_r$ of $\text{Cl}_2$. This is a common slip of confusing the halogens. Fluorine is $\text{F}_2$ with $M_r = 19.0 \times 2 = 38.0$.
options.B: Correct. One mole of $\text{F}_2$ has mass $38.0\text{ g}$ and occupies about $25.35\text{ dm}^3$ at $305\text{ K}$ and $100000\text{ Pa}$, giving $38.0 / 25.35 = 1.5\text{ g dm}^{-3}$.
options.C: Incorrect. $1.6\text{ g dm}^{-3}$ results if you round $A_r$ of F up to $20$ and use $M_r = 40$ for $\text{F}_2$. Always use $19.0$ for F, so $M_r = 38.0$.
options.D: Incorrect. $1.7\text{ g dm}^{-3}$ is the trap of using $273\text{ K}$ (0 degrees C) instead of $305\text{ K}$. A lower temperature gives a smaller molar volume ($\approx 22.7\text{ dm}^3$) and so an artificially high density of $38.0/22.7 \approx 1.67$.
